questions.text: An analyst accidentally deletes a critical object from an S3 bucket and causes hours of rework. The team wants Amazon S3 to preserve historical variants of each object so previous versions can be restored after accidental overwrite or deletion. Which S3 feature should be enabled?
questions.explanation: S3 Versioning preserves multiple versions of an object. Deleting a versioned object normally creates a delete marker, allowing previous versions to remain recoverable.
questions.hint: Think of the feature that turns each object change into a recoverable version rather than permanently replacing the previous copy.
optionRationales: S3 Versioning preserves multiple versions of an object. Deleting a versioned object normally creates a delete marker, allowing previous versions to remain recoverable.
S3 Transfer Acceleration improves long-distance transfer performance and does not preserve historical object versions.
S3 Lifecycle rules automate transitions and expirations for cost management and are not the primary accidental-overwrite recovery feature.
S3 Event Notifications inform other services about object events but do not restore or preserve deleted object content by themselves.

questions.text: Two teams in the same company use separate AWS VPCs, one for a financial system and one for a data lake, and need applications to communicate using private IP addresses without traffic traversing the public internet. Which AWS networking feature creates a direct private connection between the two VPCs?
options: An Internet Gateway in each VPC
questions.explanation: VPC Peering creates private network connectivity between two VPCs so resources can communicate using private IP addresses without routing through the public internet.
questions.hint: Think of the native peering capability that allows two VPCs to communicate directly through private addressing.
optionRationales: VPC Peering creates private network connectivity between two VPCs so resources can communicate using private IP addresses without routing through the public internet.
Internet Gateways provide public internet connectivity and do not create the private VPC-to-VPC path required here.
AWS Direct Connect links an on-premises network to AWS through dedicated connectivity; it is not primarily the mechanism for directly connecting two VPCs.
Route 53 Resolver provides DNS resolution capabilities and does not itself create the network path between VPCs.

questions.text: An industrial company needs to connect its on-premises data center to AWS. The operation requires consistent bandwidth and predictable stable latency for large daily data transfers, and the company can accept a provisioning lead time of several weeks. Compared with AWS Site-to-Site VPN, which option is the better fit and why?
options: AWS Site-to-Site VPN because dedicated connections cannot support large data transfers
AWS Site-to-Site VPN because it provides the highest guaranteed bandwidth in the AWS connectivity portfolio
AWS Direct Connect because it provides dedicated private connectivity with more consistent network performance than internet-based VPN connectivity
AWS Direct Connect because it is provisioned instantly with no physical dependencies
questions.explanation: AWS Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connectivity between a customer location and AWS and is designed for workloads that benefit from more consistent bandwidth and latency than internet-based connectivity, although provisioning can take longer.
questions.hint: Compare encrypted connectivity over the public internet with a dedicated network connection. Which one is designed for consistency at large sustained volumes?
optionRationales: AWS Direct Connect establishes dedicated network connectivity between a customer location and AWS and is designed for workloads that benefit from more consistent bandwidth and latency than internet-based connectivity, although provisioning can take longer.
Site-to-Site VPN uses encrypted tunnels over internet connectivity and therefore remains subject to internet-path variability, even though it can be provisioned more quickly.
AWS Direct Connect is specifically used for dedicated high-capacity connectivity and large regular data transfers, so the statement that it cannot support large transfers is incorrect.
AWS Direct Connect can involve physical circuit provisioning and is not generally an instant no-dependency connectivity option.

questions.text: A news portal uses Amazon RDS and experiences slowdowns during traffic peaks because readers generate a very large number of read queries while writes are relatively infrequent. The team wants to scale READ capacity without changing the primary database instance. Which RDS feature addresses this requirement?
options: Increase provisioned storage on the instance
questions.explanation: RDS Read Replicas are asynchronous replicas that can serve read traffic and help scale read-heavy workloads horizontally without placing all read queries on the primary database instance.
questions.hint: Differentiate the two common RDS concepts: one primarily supports high availability and failover; the other scales read queries.
optionRationales: RDS Read Replicas are asynchronous replicas that can serve read traffic and help scale read-heavy workloads horizontally without placing all read queries on the primary database instance.
A standard Multi-AZ standby is primarily designed for high availability and automatic failover rather than serving application read traffic.
Snapshots are point-in-time backup artifacts used for recovery and do not distribute live query load.
Increasing storage capacity increases available database storage but does not directly add independent read-processing endpoints.

questions.text: A fintech company needs a relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL but wants a cloud-native architecture with high throughput, distributed auto-growing storage, and multiple copies of data across three Availability Zones. Which AWS database service was designed specifically for these characteristics?
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL and uses a distributed storage architecture designed for high performance, automatic storage growth, and replication across multiple Availability Zones.
questions.hint: Think of AWS's cloud-native relational database known for compatibility with both MySQL and PostgreSQL and a distributed multi-AZ storage layer.
optionRationales: Amazon Aurora is a cloud-native relational database compatible with MySQL and PostgreSQL and uses a distributed storage architecture designed for high performance, automatic storage growth, and replication across multiple Availability Zones.
Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL key-value and document database and is not MySQL/PostgreSQL compatible.
Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse optimized for analytics rather than a transactional MySQL/PostgreSQL-compatible relational database.
Amazon Neptune is a graph database for highly connected datasets and does not provide MySQL or PostgreSQL compatibility.

questions.text: A retail BI team needs to run complex analytical SQL queries, aggregations, joins, and historical reports over petabytes of structured sales data using standard SQL and business-intelligence tools. Which AWS service is the appropriate managed data warehouse for this analytical workload?
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift is AWS's managed data warehouse designed for large-scale analytical workloads and integrates with SQL-based analytics and business-intelligence tools.
questions.hint: Petabytes plus SQL plus BI reporting points to the data-warehouse category. Identify the AWS service in that category.
optionRationales: Amazon Redshift is AWS's managed data warehouse designed for large-scale analytical workloads and integrates with SQL-based analytics and business-intelligence tools.
Amazon RDS is primarily optimized for transactional relational workloads rather than petabyte-scale analytical warehousing.
Amazon DynamoDB excels at low-latency NoSQL access patterns and is not designed for relational joins and large ad hoc analytical SQL queries.
Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory cache used to accelerate applications and is not a persistent analytical data warehouse.

questions.text: A recipe website repeatedly runs the same database queries, such as the day's most popular recipes, and unnecessarily overloads Amazon RDS. The architect wants an in-memory cache layer compatible with Redis or Memcached to serve repeated reads with very low latency and reduce database load. Which managed AWS service provides this layer?
questions.explanation: Amazon ElastiCache is AWS's managed in-memory caching service and supports engines designed for high-speed caching workloads such as Redis-compatible and Memcached environments.
questions.hint: The Redis and Memcached names point directly to AWS's managed in-memory cache service.
optionRationales: Amazon ElastiCache is AWS's managed in-memory caching service and supports engines designed for high-speed caching workloads such as Redis-compatible and Memcached environments.
DAX is an in-memory cache specifically designed for DynamoDB rather than a general cache layer for relational databases such as RDS.
Amazon CloudFront caches web content at edge locations for end users rather than database query results between an application and its database.
Amazon EFS is a shared elastic file system and is not a sub-millisecond in-memory database cache.

questions.text: A startup publishes a serverless API with AWS Lambda and wants to estimate costs. Which statement correctly describes the AWS Lambda pricing model?
options: Charges are based on the number of requests and execution duration relative to configured resources, with no compute charge while code is not running
AWS Lambda is completely free for any volume of executions
A fixed monthly fee is charged for every function created regardless of usage
Billing is based on reserved server hours like EC2 instances
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda is generally billed according to requests and compute duration based on the resources allocated to the function. When a function is not executing, there is no normal Lambda compute-duration charge for that idle time.
questions.hint: In serverless computing, the core pricing idea is that compute charges follow actual function execution rather than idle server time.
optionRationales: AWS Lambda is generally billed according to requests and compute duration based on the resources allocated to the function. When a function is not executing, there is no normal Lambda compute-duration charge for that idle time.
There is no normal fixed compute fee simply for keeping an idle Lambda function deployed.
The serverless model avoids reserving ordinary server hours for function execution; billing follows actual invocations and compute consumption.
AWS Lambda has free-tier allowances, but usage beyond applicable free allowances can be billed normally.

questions.text: A team builds business logic in AWS Lambda functions and needs to expose it through a public REST API with authentication support, request throttling, API lifecycle controls, and monitoring. Which managed service acts as the API front door for these functions?
questions.explanation: Amazon API Gateway creates, publishes, secures, monitors, and manages REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs at scale and integrates natively with AWS Lambda for serverless architectures.
questions.hint: Think of the AWS service whose name literally describes a gateway for APIs.
optionRationales: Amazon API Gateway creates, publishes, secures, monitors, and manages REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs at scale and integrates natively with AWS Lambda for serverless architectures.
An Application Load Balancer can route requests to Lambda in some architectures but does not provide the complete API-management feature set described in this scenario.
Amazon Route 53 provides DNS resolution and routing and does not manage API authentication, throttling, and lifecycle controls.
AWS Step Functions orchestrates workflows and state machines rather than exposing Lambda functions as managed public REST APIs.

questions.text: An e-commerce platform built with microservices needs a load balancer that routes HTTPS requests based on application content: calls to '/cart' should go to one container group while requests for 'api.store.com' should go to another, with header inspection and native support for container targets. Which Elastic Load Balancing type fits these requirements?
questions.explanation: An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and supports routing based on HTTP/HTTPS attributes such as URL paths, hostnames, and headers, making it well suited to containerized microservices.
questions.hint: Routing based on URL and hostname requires a load balancer that understands the application layer and HTTP requests.
optionRationales: An Application Load Balancer operates at Layer 7 and supports routing based on HTTP/HTTPS attributes such as URL paths, hostnames, and headers, making it well suited to containerized microservices.
A Network Load Balancer operates primarily at Layer 4 for high-performance connection handling and does not perform content-based HTTP routing.
A Gateway Load Balancer distributes network traffic to virtual appliances such as firewalls and security inspection systems rather than routing HTTP microservices by path.
A Classic Load Balancer is a previous-generation option and lacks the modern content-routing capabilities of the ALB.

questions.text: A global application runs in two AWS Regions: São Paulo and Frankfurt. Each user should be sent to the Region expected to provide the fastest network response based on AWS latency measurements rather than simply on geographic distance. Which Amazon Route 53 routing policy implements this behavior?
questions.explanation: Latency-based routing directs users to the AWS endpoint that Route 53 determines will provide the lowest latency, using network-performance measurements rather than geographic boundaries alone.
questions.hint: The clue is measured network performance. Which Route 53 policy chooses the fastest endpoint rather than the closest point on a map?
optionRationales: Latency-based routing directs users to the AWS endpoint that Route 53 determines will provide the lowest latency, using network-performance measurements rather than geographic boundaries alone.
Geolocation routing makes decisions according to the user's geographic origin, which is not always the same as the lowest-latency network path.
Weighted routing splits traffic according to configured proportions rather than per-user network latency.
Failover routing selects primary or secondary endpoints based on health for active-passive recovery rather than optimizing each user's response time.

questions.text: A team wants to release a new website version gradually: 10% of users should be directed to the new environment and 90% should remain on the current environment, with those percentages adjusted over the week as confidence increases. Which Amazon Route 53 routing policy supports this gradual traffic release?
questions.explanation: Weighted routing assigns relative weights to DNS records so traffic can be distributed in controlled proportions, which is useful for canary releases and DNS-based A/B testing.
questions.hint: The requirement is to distribute traffic according to administrator-defined percentages. Which policy uses weights?
optionRationales: Weighted routing assigns relative weights to DNS records so traffic can be distributed in controlled proportions, which is useful for canary releases and DNS-based A/B testing.
Latency-based routing selects the endpoint expected to provide the lowest latency rather than honoring fixed deployment percentages.
Failover routing sends traffic to a primary endpoint until health checks trigger use of a secondary endpoint and does not provide adjustable percentage splitting.
Simple routing does not provide the controlled weighted distribution required for this rollout.

questions.text: A streaming company wants to improve the global experience of two products: a catalog of cacheable videos and images, and a real-time TCP chat service that cannot be cached but needs static global IP addresses and optimized routing over the AWS network. Which services fit these products, respectively?
options: AWS Global Accelerator for cacheable content and Amazon CloudFront for TCP traffic
AWS Direct Connect for both cases
Amazon CloudFront for cacheable content and AWS Global Accelerator for real-time TCP traffic
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that caches content at edge locations, while AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and optimizes non-cacheable TCP/UDP traffic paths across the AWS global network.
questions.hint: Separate what can be cached at the edge from what simply needs a faster and more stable global network path.
optionRationales: Amazon CloudFront is a CDN that caches content at edge locations, while AWS Global Accelerator provides static anycast IP addresses and optimizes non-cacheable TCP/UDP traffic paths across the AWS global network.
This reverses the services: CloudFront performs edge caching, while Global Accelerator optimizes network paths without acting as a content cache.
Amazon Route 53 provides DNS routing but does not cache content or provide the same anycast static-IP traffic acceleration service.
AWS Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity from customer networks to AWS and is unrelated to global end-user content delivery or internet traffic acceleration.

questions.text: A company is evaluating AWS container orchestrators. The team already uses Kubernetes on premises with manifests, Helm charts, and CNCF ecosystem tools that must continue to work without rewriting. Between Amazon ECS and Amazon EKS, which choice is appropriate and why?
options: Amazon EKS because it removes every concept of clusters and control planes
Amazon EKS because it provides managed Kubernetes and preserves compatibility with Kubernetes manifests and ecosystem tooling
Amazon ECS because it is the only AWS orchestrator that supports Docker containers
Amazon ECS because Kubernetes manifests are automatically converted into ECS task definitions
questions.explanation: Amazon EKS provides managed Kubernetes and is the appropriate choice when existing Kubernetes APIs, manifests, and ecosystem tooling need to remain compatible.
questions.hint: When the requirement is compatibility with an existing Kubernetes ecosystem, which AWS orchestrator speaks Kubernetes natively?
optionRationales: Amazon EKS provides managed Kubernetes and is the appropriate choice when existing Kubernetes APIs, manifests, and ecosystem tooling need to remain compatible.
Both ECS and EKS can run OCI containers; the key difference is the orchestration API and ecosystem, with EKS providing Kubernetes compatibility.
There is no automatic general-purpose conversion of Kubernetes manifests into ECS task definitions that removes migration work.
Amazon EKS still uses Kubernetes clusters; AWS manages the Kubernetes control plane rather than eliminating the cluster model entirely.

questions.text: An online store knows that every day at 8:00 PM a predictable traffic peak begins and lasts until 11:00 PM, requiring twice as many EC2 instances. The team wants Auto Scaling to increase capacity shortly before 8:00 PM and reduce it after 11:00 PM every day without waiting for CPU metrics to rise. Which scaling approach fits this pattern?
options: Simple scaling based on a memory alarm
Manual scaling from the console every night
questions.explanation: Scheduled Scaling adjusts Auto Scaling capacity at predefined times and is well suited to recurring predictable demand patterns because capacity can be changed before the load arrives.
questions.hint: If the peak has a known time every day, which scaling method uses the clock rather than waiting for a metric threshold?
optionRationales: Scheduled Scaling adjusts Auto Scaling capacity at predefined times and is well suited to recurring predictable demand patterns because capacity can be changed before the load arrives.
Target Tracking responds to measured load and therefore reacts after the workload changes rather than using the known recurring schedule.
Manual nightly scaling is operationally fragile and unnecessary when the traffic pattern is predictable and recurring.
Reactive alarm-based policies wait for metrics to cross thresholds and do not use the known daily schedule proactively.

questions.text: In an order architecture, the 'order confirmed' event must be delivered to billing, logistics, and email systems at the same time, while each system must process events at its own pace with a durable buffer if it becomes unavailable. The architect proposes publishing the event to a topic that feeds one queue per consumer. Which service combination implements this fan-out-with-buffer pattern?
options: Amazon SQS publishing to multiple Amazon SNS topics
AWS Step Functions running all three systems sequentially
One SQS queue shared by all three consumer systems
Amazon SNS publishing to multiple Amazon SQS queues subscribed to the topic
questions.explanation: A common fan-out pattern uses an Amazon SNS topic to distribute each published event to multiple subscribed Amazon SQS queues. Each queue gives its consumer an independent durable buffer.
questions.hint: Think of one publisher broadcasting to many independent inboxes: publish/subscribe in front and durable queues behind it.
optionRationales: A common fan-out pattern uses an Amazon SNS topic to distribute each published event to multiple subscribed Amazon SQS queues. Each queue gives its consumer an independent durable buffer.
The direction is reversed: SQS queues do not normally publish fan-out messages into SNS topics; SNS distributes published events to subscribers such as queues.
With one shared queue, competing consumers would each process different messages instead of every system receiving its own copy.
AWS Step Functions can coordinate workflows but would couple the systems into an orchestrated execution rather than provide independent durable consumer buffers.

questions.text: A banking system sends transactions to a queue and requires two guarantees: messages must be processed in the exact order in which they were sent, and duplicate processing must be prevented. Which Amazon SQS feature is designed for these requirements?
options: SQS Standard queues because they guarantee strict ordering by default
Use Amazon SNS instead of SQS
SQS FIFO queues with ordering and message deduplication
Increase the Visibility Timeout of a Standard queue
questions.explanation: SQS FIFO queues are designed for workloads that require message ordering and deduplication capabilities, making them suitable for cases where sequence and duplicate prevention are important.
questions.hint: The queue type's acronym means first in, first out and directly refers to preserving order.
optionRationales: SQS FIFO queues are designed for workloads that require message ordering and deduplication capabilities, making them suitable for cases where sequence and duplicate prevention are important.
SQS Standard queues provide at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering rather than the strict FIFO behavior required here.
Visibility Timeout helps prevent another consumer from immediately receiving an in-flight message but does not by itself provide FIFO ordering and deduplication semantics.
Amazon SNS is a publish/subscribe notification service and does not replace the durable FIFO queue semantics required for this processing pattern.

questions.text: An event-driven architecture needs a central bus that receives events from custom applications, AWS services, and partner SaaS applications and uses content-based rules to route each event to the appropriate target such as Lambda, SQS, or Step Functions. Which AWS service provides this event bus?
questions.explanation: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that accepts events from AWS services, custom applications, and supported SaaS sources and routes them to targets according to event-pattern rules.
questions.hint: Think of the AWS event bridge that connects internal, AWS, and SaaS event sources to multiple targets through routing rules.
optionRationales: Amazon EventBridge is a serverless event bus that accepts events from AWS services, custom applications, and supported SaaS sources and routes them to targets according to event-pattern rules.
Amazon SQS is a message queue for decoupling producers and consumers and is not the same content-routing event-bus model with broad SaaS event integrations.
AWS Direct Connect is a dedicated networking service and has no role in application event routing.
Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose continuously delivers streaming data to destinations such as storage and analytics services and is not a general event bus for discrete application events.

questions.text: A credit-approval process involves several Lambda functions running in sequence, conditional decisions, automatic retries after failures, and an auditable visual history of each execution. The team does not want to code this coordination manually inside the functions. Which AWS service orchestrates this workflow?
options: Amazon SQS with several chained queues
questions.explanation: AWS Step Functions orchestrates workflows using state machines and can coordinate Lambda functions and other AWS services with sequencing, conditions, retries, error handling, and execution history.
questions.hint: Think of the AWS state-machine service that represents a workflow as an executable sequence of steps.
optionRationales: AWS Step Functions orchestrates workflows using state machines and can coordinate Lambda functions and other AWS services with sequencing, conditions, retries, error handling, and execution history.
Chaining SQS queues would still require the application to implement much of the state, branching, retry, and coordination logic manually.
EventBridge Scheduler invokes targets on schedules and does not orchestrate multi-step conditional business workflows.
AWS CodePipeline orchestrates software delivery stages such as build, test, and deployment rather than runtime business workflows between application functions.

questions.text: A media-processing cluster needs dozens of EC2 instances distributed across multiple Availability Zones to read and write the same files concurrently through a shared, elastic, managed network file system with Linux POSIX semantics. Which AWS storage service fits this requirement?
questions.explanation: Amazon EFS provides a managed elastic network file system that can be mounted by many Linux clients across multiple Availability Zones and automatically grows and shrinks as files are added and removed.
questions.hint: The key requirement is many instances mounting the same shared file system across multiple Availability Zones.
optionRationales: Amazon EFS provides a managed elastic network file system that can be mounted by many Linux clients across multiple Availability Zones and automatically grows and shrinks as files are added and removed.
EBS volumes are block storage resources scoped to an Availability Zone and do not provide the broad multi-AZ shared file-system behavior described here.
Instance Store is local ephemeral storage tied to the underlying host and cannot serve as a shared multi-instance network file system.
S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval is an object archival storage class and is not mounted as a shared POSIX file system for real-time access.

questions.text: An administrator needs point-in-time backups of EBS volumes used by critical EC2 instances. The backups should be incremental, durable, and usable to restore new EBS volumes in another Availability Zone. Which AWS capability provides this?
options: An AMI without an associated snapshot
S3 Versioning applied to the volume
Read replicas for the EBS volume
questions.explanation: EBS Snapshots are point-in-time incremental backups of EBS volumes. They are managed durably by AWS and can be used to create new EBS volumes in Availability Zones within the Region, and snapshots can also be copied across Regions.
questions.hint: Think of the native incremental snapshot mechanism for block volumes that can restore new volumes.
optionRationales: EBS Snapshots are point-in-time incremental backups of EBS volumes. They are managed durably by AWS and can be used to create new EBS volumes in Availability Zones within the Region, and snapshots can also be copied across Regions.
There is no EBS read-replica feature analogous to relational database read replicas.
S3 Versioning applies to S3 objects and not directly to EBS block volumes.
EBS-backed AMIs rely on snapshots and represent an EC2 instance image rather than replacing the underlying volume snapshot mechanism.

questions.text: A network of clinics keeps on-premises systems that write exams to office file servers but wants to extend storage to AWS in a hybrid architecture. Local applications should continue using standard file protocols such as NFS or SMB with low-latency local caching while the data is stored durably in Amazon S3. Which AWS service enables this hybrid integration?
questions.explanation: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments with AWS storage. File Gateway supports file access through protocols such as NFS and SMB with local caching while storing data in Amazon S3.
questions.hint: Think of the AWS storage gateway that sits in the customer environment and bridges familiar file protocols with cloud storage.
optionRationales: AWS Storage Gateway connects on-premises environments with AWS storage. File Gateway supports file access through protocols such as NFS and SMB with local caching while storing data in Amazon S3.
AWS Snowball Edge is primarily a physical device for large-scale data transfer and edge computing and is not the continuous file-gateway integration described here.
Amazon EFS is a managed file system for AWS workloads and does not by itself provide the on-premises gateway with local cache and S3-backed object persistence described in the scenario.
Amazon WorkDocs is a user document collaboration service rather than hybrid storage infrastructure for existing applications.

questions.text: An EC2 instance uses two types of storage: an EBS root volume and Instance Store disks provided by the underlying host. What happens to the data in each when the instance is stopped and later started again?
options: Both storage types preserve data indefinitely
EBS volume data normally persists, while Instance Store data is lost
Both storage types lose data when the instance stops
Instance Store data persists while EBS data is deleted automatically
questions.explanation: EBS provides persistent network block storage that survives normal instance stop/start cycles, while Instance Store is ephemeral storage tied to the host and does not persist through stop/start in the same way.
questions.hint: One storage type is persistent network block storage; the other is temporary storage physically associated with the host.
optionRationales: EBS provides persistent network block storage that survives normal instance stop/start cycles, while Instance Store is ephemeral storage tied to the host and does not persist through stop/start in the same way.
EBS is designed to retain data independently of an EC2 instance's normal stop/start cycle.
Instance Store is ephemeral and data can be lost when the instance is stopped, terminated, or moved away from the underlying host.
The behavior is the reverse of the final option: persistence is the defining EBS property, while Instance Store is ephemeral.

questions.text: A development team wants to deploy a Java web application to AWS with minimal infrastructure effort: upload the application package and let the service automatically provision instances, load balancing, Auto Scaling, and monitoring while still allowing access to the underlying resources for fine tuning. Which AWS service provides this experience?
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys application code and automatically provisions supporting AWS resources such as EC2 instances, load balancing, Auto Scaling, and monitoring while keeping the resources accessible for customization.
questions.hint: Think of AWS's application-platform service where the team deploys code and the service builds the surrounding environment.
optionRationales: AWS Elastic Beanstalk deploys application code and automatically provisions supporting AWS resources such as EC2 instances, load balancing, Auto Scaling, and monitoring while keeping the resources accessible for customization.
AWS CloudFormation provisions infrastructure from declarative templates written by the user rather than inferring an application environment from an uploaded application package.
Amazon Lightsail provides simplified virtual private servers and related services but is not the same automatic full application-environment platform described here.
AWS Systems Manager focuses on operating and managing existing resources and is not an application deployment platform that automatically builds the full environment from application code.

questions.text: An infrastructure team wants to define its entire AWS architecture, including VPCs, instances, databases, and permissions, in declarative text files versioned in Git so identical environments can be recreated repeatably in other accounts and Regions. Which native AWS service implements this infrastructure-as-code practice?
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation provisions and manages AWS resources from declarative YAML or JSON templates organized into stacks, enabling infrastructure definitions to be version-controlled and reproduced consistently.
questions.hint: Think of the AWS service that transforms a YAML or JSON infrastructure template into a stack of AWS resources.
optionRationales: AWS CloudFormation provisions and manages AWS resources from declarative YAML or JSON templates organized into stacks, enabling infrastructure definitions to be version-controlled and reproduced consistently.
AWS Config records and evaluates the configuration of existing resources for compliance but does not provision complete infrastructure from declarative templates.
An AMI captures an EC2 machine image and cannot describe complete architectures with networking, databases, and permissions.
A Git repository can store infrastructure templates, but CloudFormation is the AWS service that interprets the templates and provisions the resources.

questions.text: A monitoring system must fulfill two different roles: first, track instance performance metrics such as CPU and network with alarms and dashboards; second, record who created, modified, or deleted AWS resources through API calls for audit purposes. Which services fulfill roles one and two, respectively?
options: Amazon CloudWatch for metrics and alarms; AWS CloudTrail for API-call auditing
AWS CloudTrail for metrics and alarms; Amazon CloudWatch for API auditing
AWS Health Dashboard for both roles
Amazon Inspector for metrics; AWS Config for API calls
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch provides observability capabilities such as metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards, while AWS CloudTrail records AWS account activity and API calls for auditing.
questions.hint: Remember the pair: CloudWatch watches performance; CloudTrail follows the trail of who did what.
optionRationales: Amazon CloudWatch provides observability capabilities such as metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards, while AWS CloudTrail records AWS account activity and API calls for auditing.
This reverses the two services: CloudTrail does not provide ordinary performance dashboards, and CloudWatch is not the account API audit trail.
Amazon Inspector assesses workload vulnerabilities and AWS Config tracks resource configuration, so neither pair matches performance dashboards plus API auditing.
AWS Health Dashboard reports AWS service health events affecting the account and is not a replacement for either performance metrics or API audit logging.

questions.text: Finance leadership wants to estimate how much the company will spend on AWS over the next three months. An analyst opens AWS Cost Explorer and uses a feature that projects future costs based on historical account-consumption patterns. Which Cost Explorer capability is being used?
options: A financial compliance report certified by external auditors
Simulation of hypothetical architectures that do not yet exist in the account
Cost forecast, which projects future spending from historical usage
Automatic blocking of new resources whenever the projection exceeds budget
questions.explanation: AWS Cost Explorer includes forecasting capabilities that use historical cost and usage patterns to project future spending and support financial planning.
questions.hint: Differentiate estimating an architecture that does not exist yet from forecasting the future based on actual historical spending.
optionRationales: AWS Cost Explorer includes forecasting capabilities that use historical cost and usage patterns to project future spending and support financial planning.
Cost Explorer is not an external-auditor compliance reporting service; AWS compliance reports are available through services such as AWS Artifact.
AWS Pricing Calculator is used to estimate hypothetical architectures before deployment, while Cost Explorer analyzes actual historical and forecasted account spending.
Cost Explorer is an analysis tool. Budget thresholds and automated budget actions belong to AWS Budgets rather than the Cost Explorer forecast itself.

questions.text: A FinOps team needs highly granular AWS billing data, including detailed line items by resource and time period, tags, and applied discounts, delivered automatically to Amazon S3 for analysis with its own BI tooling. Which AWS cost-management capability provides this detailed billing dataset?
options: The monthly PDF invoice in the Billing console
questions.explanation: AWS Cost and Usage Reports provide detailed cost and usage line items and can deliver billing data to Amazon S3 for analysis with AWS analytics services or external BI tools.
questions.hint: Think of the detailed AWS cost-and-usage dataset commonly delivered into S3 for downstream analysis.
optionRationales: AWS Cost and Usage Reports provide detailed cost and usage line items and can deliver billing data to Amazon S3 for analysis with AWS analytics services or external BI tools.
AWS Cost Explorer provides interactive cost visualization and analysis but is not the same detailed S3-delivered billing dataset.
AWS Budgets monitors financial thresholds and sends alerts rather than producing the complete detailed billing dataset.
A monthly invoice summarizes charges for payment and does not provide the same structured resource-level analytical dataset.

questions.text: A new AWS customer wants to explore cloud services in 2026 while controlling the risk of unexpected charges. Which statement correctly describes the current AWS Free Tier experience for new customers?
options: Every new AWS account receives all services free for exactly 12 months with no credit limit
Free usage is limited only to compute, storage, and networking services

New customers can choose a Free plan that lasts up to six months or until Free Tier credits are exhausted, receive initial credits with opportunities to earn additional credits, and can also use eligible Always Free offers within their limits
The Free Tier consists only of Reserved Instance, volume, and Spot pricing discounts
questions.explanation: The current AWS Free Tier lets new customers choose a Free plan that ends after up to six months or when Free Tier credits are exhausted, whichever happens first. New customers receive initial AWS credits and can earn additional credits through eligible activities, while eligible Always Free service offers continue to provide monthly free usage limits.
questions.hint: The modern Free Tier combines a time-limited Free account plan with credits and ongoing Always Free service allowances, rather than the older blanket 12-month model.
optionRationales: The current program is not a blanket twelve-month free period for every service. AWS introduced a Free plan based on credits and a maximum six-month exploration period for new customers.
AWS Free Tier spans services from many categories and is not restricted to only compute, storage, and networking.

New customers can choose a Free plan that ends after up to six months or when Free Tier credits are exhausted, receive AWS credits, and retain access to eligible Always Free offers within their monthly limits.
Reserved Instances, Savings Plans, volume tiers, and Spot pricing are paid-use discount mechanisms and are not the definition of AWS Free Tier.

questions.text: After activating cost allocation tags, a company's finance team can view AWS spending broken down by tags such as 'cost-center' and 'project'. Which financial-management practice does this capability directly enable?
options: Chargeback/showback: attributing cloud costs to the departments or projects responsible for the consumption
Automatic reduction of AWS rates for tagged resources
Encryption of billing reports separately for each department
Automatic deletion of the most expensive resources in each department
questions.explanation: Cost allocation tags help organizations attribute cloud spending to teams, departments, products, or projects, enabling showback and internal chargeback practices and strengthening financial accountability.
questions.hint: When every cloud cost can be associated with an owner, which internal cost-attribution practice becomes possible?
optionRationales: Cost allocation tags help organizations attribute cloud spending to teams, departments, products, or projects, enabling showback and internal chargeback practices and strengthening financial accountability.
Cost allocation tags categorize spending but do not automatically delete resources.
Tags do not reduce AWS service prices; discounts come from pricing and commitment mechanisms rather than tagging alone.
Cost allocation tags provide reporting dimensions and are unrelated to encryption of financial documents.

questions.text: A company needs a third-party application firewall available as a virtual appliance. Instead of negotiating directly with the vendor and installing it manually, the team wants to discover, evaluate, subscribe to, and deploy the product on AWS with charges integrated into the AWS bill. Which channel provides this experience?
questions.explanation: AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog of third-party software, including SaaS products, AMIs, containers, and related solutions, with procurement and billing integrated into AWS for supported listings.
questions.hint: Think of AWS's marketplace for purchasing and deploying third-party software with integrated billing.
optionRationales: AWS Marketplace is a digital catalog of third-party software, including SaaS products, AMIs, containers, and related solutions, with procurement and billing integrated into AWS for supported listings.
AWS Artifact provides AWS compliance reports and agreements rather than third-party software procurement.
AWS Service Catalog helps an organization distribute its own approved cloud products internally; AWS Marketplace is the broader vendor marketplace.
AWS Organizations manages multi-account governance and consolidated billing rather than software discovery and procurement.

questions.text: A CIO must present a fair comparison between keeping an on-premises data center and moving workloads to AWS. The analysis should compare total cost of ownership (TCO), not just server purchase prices. Which on-premises costs should be included?
options: Only the purchase price of physical servers
Direct and indirect costs such as hardware, software, facilities, power, cooling, networking, and data-center operations staff
questions.explanation: TCO includes the full cost of owning and operating infrastructure, including hardware, software, facilities, energy, cooling, connectivity, and personnel, rather than only the acquisition price of servers.
questions.hint: TCO means total cost of ownership: include everything required for the infrastructure to exist and operate, not just the obvious hardware purchase.
optionRationales: TCO includes the full cost of owning and operating infrastructure, including hardware, software, facilities, energy, cooling, connectivity, and personnel, rather than only the acquisition price of servers.
Counting only server hardware omits major facilities and operating expenses and would distort the comparison.
Personnel is one part of TCO, but capital and operating infrastructure costs must also be included.
Software licensing is only one component; fair TCO analysis also includes hardware, facilities, energy, networking, and operations.

questions.text: A research company runs nightly image-rendering batches that can be interrupted and resumed without business impact. The team wants to use spare EC2 capacity at very large discounts compared with On-Demand pricing and accepts that AWS may interrupt the instances. Which EC2 purchasing model matches this strategy?
questions.explanation: EC2 Spot Instances use spare AWS compute capacity at deep discounts and are designed for interruption-tolerant workloads such as batch processing, rendering, testing, and other flexible compute jobs.
questions.hint: Maximum savings plus the possibility of interruption points to EC2's spare-capacity purchasing model.
optionRationales: EC2 Spot Instances use spare AWS compute capacity at deep discounts and are designed for interruption-tolerant workloads such as batch processing, rendering, testing, and other flexible compute jobs.
On-Demand Instances provide flexible usage without a long-term commitment but use normal On-Demand pricing rather than the deep spare-capacity discount described here.
Dedicated Hosts allocate entire physical servers for licensing or compliance needs and are not a low-cost spare-capacity model.
Capacity Reservations reserve EC2 capacity in a specific Availability Zone but do not provide the Spot discount mechanism for interruptible spare capacity.

questions.text: A company compares the two main Savings Plans types before making a three-year commitment. Its primary workload is stable and will remain on the same EC2 instance family in the same Region, and the goal is to obtain the larger discount available in exchange for giving up flexibility. Which option best fits this scenario?
options: Compute Savings Plans because they always provide the largest possible discount in every scenario
EC2 Instance Savings Plans, which trade flexibility for potentially greater savings by committing to an instance family in a Region
On-Demand pricing combined with cost allocation tags
Spot Instances with a three-year commitment
questions.explanation: EC2 Instance Savings Plans can provide greater discounts than the more flexible Compute Savings Plans when an organization is comfortable committing to a specific EC2 instance family in a Region.
questions.hint: The Savings Plans tradeoff is flexibility versus discount: the more specific commitment can provide the larger discount when the workload is predictable.
optionRationales: EC2 Instance Savings Plans can provide greater discounts than the more flexible Compute Savings Plans when an organization is comfortable committing to a specific EC2 instance family in a Region.

Compute Savings Plans offer broader flexibility across eligible compute usage, including changes in family and Region, and that flexibility can come with a lower maximum discount than the more specific EC2 Instance plan.
Spot Instances use interruptible spare capacity and do not represent a three-year spend commitment for a stable primary workload.
Cost allocation tags help attribute costs but do not create a pricing discount by themselves.

questions.text: A global organization considers AWS strategically critical and wants the highest level of expert support, including a designated Technical Account Manager (TAM), proactive architectural and operational guidance, and a response target of up to 15 minutes for business-critical systems that are down. Which AWS Support plan provides these capabilities?
questions.explanation: AWS Enterprise Support provides designated TAM engagement, proactive guidance, and the shortest response targets for business-critical incidents, including a 15-minute response target for the most severe business-critical system-down cases.
questions.hint: A designated TAM plus the 15-minute business-critical response target identifies the highest Enterprise support tier.
optionRationales: AWS Enterprise Support provides designated TAM engagement, proactive guidance, and the shortest response targets for business-critical incidents, including a 15-minute response target for the most severe business-critical system-down cases.
AWS Business Support provides 24/7 technical support for production workloads but does not provide the full designated-TAM Enterprise experience described here.
AWS Enterprise On-Ramp is being phased out and historically provided an intermediate enterprise support experience rather than the full designated Enterprise Support model required by this scenario.
AWS Developer Support is designed for development and testing use cases and does not match a mission-critical global enterprise support requirement.

questions.text: An AWS Organizations environment has account A with unused matching Reserved Instance benefits while account B runs equivalent On-Demand EC2 instances. With consolidated billing and discount sharing enabled, what happens to the unused reservation benefit?
options: The benefit is always lost because Reserved Instance discounts can apply only to the purchasing account
Eligible matching usage in account B can receive the shared Reserved Instance discount benefit
AWS automatically refunds unused reservations on the next invoice
The EC2 instances in account B are physically moved into account A
questions.explanation: With consolidated billing, eligible Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discount benefits can be shared across accounts in an organization when discount sharing is enabled, allowing matching usage in another account to consume an otherwise unused benefit.
questions.hint: The financial discount can be shared across linked accounts; the actual EC2 resources do not move between accounts.
optionRationales: With consolidated billing, eligible Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discount benefits can be shared across accounts in an organization when discount sharing is enabled, allowing matching usage in another account to consume an otherwise unused benefit.
The benefit is not necessarily restricted to the purchasing account when consolidated billing discount sharing is enabled.
AWS does not automatically refund an unused reservation simply because the purchasing account did not consume it.
Only the billing benefit is shared; resources remain in their original AWS accounts and are not physically migrated to consume the discount.

questions.text: An operations manager wants to go beyond budget alerts: when a development environment reaches 100% of its monthly budget, AWS should automatically perform a control action such as applying a restrictive IAM policy that prevents creation of additional EC2 instances. Which capability makes this possible?
options: AWS Budgets Actions, which can trigger configured control responses when budget thresholds are reached
questions.explanation: AWS Budgets Actions can run configured automated or approval-based responses when a budget threshold is reached, including actions involving IAM policies, SCPs, and supported resource controls.
questions.hint: Look for the AWS Budgets feature that converts a passive budget alert into an actual control action.
optionRationales: AWS Budgets Actions can run configured automated or approval-based responses when a budget threshold is reached, including actions involving IAM policies, SCPs, and supported resource controls.
Cost Explorer forecasting projects future spending but does not itself apply restrictive policies to resources.
CloudWatch billing alarms can notify on billing thresholds but do not provide the integrated budget-action controls described here.
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection identifies unusual spending patterns and alerts on anomalies rather than enforcing a fixed monthly budget with configured actions.
